newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Main Palestinian-Israeli events since start of 1996.
newsitem.headline: Main Palestinian-Israeli events since start of 1996.

text.p: Following are the main events in the troubled Israeli-Palestinian peace process since the killing of the alleged mastermind of Palestinian bombing in 1996 until the latest bombing on Friday of a Tel Aviv cafe.

Jan 5, 1996 - Yahya Ayyash, known as "The Engineer" and termed the mastermind behind a wave of Islamic suicide bombings against Israel, is killed in the Gaza Strip. Islamic group Hamas vows to avenge his death, which it blames on Israel.
Jan 20 - Palestinians hold first election for president and parliament to rule in the West Bank and Gaza under peace deal with Israel. PLO chief Yasser Arafat is elected president.
Feb 25 - Two Hamas suicide bombers kill 27 people in attacks in Jerusalem and the southern Israeli town of Ashkelon. Bombings said to be in revenge for the killing of Ayyash.
March 3 - Hamas suicide bomber on a bus in Jerusalem kills 19 people. Israel declares all-out war against Hamas.
March 4 - Hamas suicide bomber kills 13 people in Tel Aviv shopping mall.
March 23 - Israel, rocked by the bombings, delays leaving Hebron, the seventh West Bank town scheduled to be handed over.
May 29 - Right-wing Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu ousts Shimon Peres in national elections.
Aug 2 - Netanyahu infuriates Palestinians by lifting a four-year freeze on West Bank Jewish settlement expansion imposed by the previous government.
Sept 24 - Israeli government opens tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem near Islamic holy site, igniting days of protests in which 61 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers die.
Sept 29 - U.S. President Bill Clinton invites Netanyahu, Arafat, Jordan's King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to White House summit that launches marathon talks on Hebron redeployment.
Dec 11 - Guerrillas from the Popular Front of the Liberation of Palestine shoot dead 12-year-old Israeli boy and his mother near the PLO-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah.
Jan 1, 1997 - An off-duty Israeli soldier fires into a market in Hebron, wounding seven Palestinians.
Jan 9 - Two bombs explode in rubbish bins in Tel Aviv, wounding at least 13 people. There is no claim of responsibility and it is unclear if the attack is political or criminal.
Jan 17 - Israel hands 80 percent of Hebron over to Palestinian administration after months of negotiations.
March 13 - Seven Israeli schoolgirls are shot dead at the Jordan River by a Jordanian soldier as tension rises in the region over Israeli plans to increase Jewish settlement.
March 18 - Israel starts building 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem despite international opposition and Palestinian warnings it could trigger violence.
March 20 - Palestinians angered by the settlement throw petrol bombs and rocks at Israeli soldiers beside Bethlehem on the outskirts of Jerusalem.
March 21 - Clashes break out between Palestinian youths and Israeli soldiers in Hebron over the East Jerusalem building.
March 21 - A bomb rips through a cafe in Tel Aviv, killing at least four people and wounding 43 in an apparent suicide attack.
